correctness.rationale: For q!=4 every oriented edge has a unique ±1 increment. Every prism square has zero signed circulation (absolute <=4 and even; no nonzero multiple of q>=5 or q3), so both rim windings coincide, integral w with qw≡n mod2 and |qw|<=n. For strict winding, a directed cycle would have length |qwm|<n|m|<=length (or zero horizontal winding), contradiction; thus induced orientation is acyclic. Differences of two equal-winding signed cocycles are an integral exact 1-cochain; a height lattice with pointwise minima and legal source-vertex ±2 recoloring is connected. Even-target parity at a vertex splits components; odd targets do not. The inspected primary Fujii et al. Theorem 5.1 maps acyclic orientation components to S1; extreme all-horizontal-sign cases yield precisely 4q isolated vertices. For q=4 twin-vertex folding reduces target to K2 and gives two components for even n. Independently enumerated Hom vertex colorings and 1-skeleton recoloring components for n=3..7, q=3..8, matching all counts and isolated cases, not the circle homotopy (which relies on primary theorem).
